frameworks.name: Domain-Specific Decision Authority
frameworks.definition: Couples working together assign decision authority by domain expertise—each person owns decisions in areas where they have superior knowledge or relationship—while reserving big strategic decisions for joint agreement.

frameworks.name: Proactive Relationship Maintenance
frameworks.definition: Preventing work-relationship degradation requires explicit verbal signaling when imbalance is noticed, with one partner ceding to the other's request rather than letting tension accumulate.

claims.text: Rory Sutherland and his wife Layla minimized romantic conflict by building an intimate work relationship first (recruiting her to join his business on day one) before developing traditional dating intimacy, requiring both parties to learn how to separate the two contexts.
claims.speaker: Rory Sutherland
conditions: couple starting a business relationship simultaneously with romantic relationship
claims.mechanism: By establishing professional context and clear expectations early, the couple could ground their relationship in shared mission before romantic expectations risked derailing work decisions.
bounded_by: Does not address couples who meet first romantically then add work later
Does not address power imbalances in decision-making

claims.text: Rory and Layla resolve work-relationship balance not by actively 'balancing' the two but by treating them as integrated; when relationship quality declines, they explicitly negotiate dedicated 'us time', and when one person notices the imbalance, the other immediately concedes rather than defensively protecting the status quo.
claims.speaker: Rory Sutherland
conditions: both parties committed to transparency about relationship need
claims.mechanism: Explicit signaling prevents silent resentment accumulation; immediate concession short-circuits defensive escalation cycles.
bounded_by: Does not apply to couples who avoid difficult conversations
Requires both parties to have equal standing to request 'us time'

claims.text: In Rory and Layla's working partnership, domain-specific authority prevents decision paralysis: Layla owns talent/hiring decisions when she knows candidates better, Rory owns marketing angles, and each defers to the other's domain expertise without requiring consensus on every operational choice.
claims.speaker: Rory Sutherland
conditions: clear domain boundaries (e.g., one owns talent/hiring, other owns strategy/marketing)
claims.mechanism: Assigning authority by domain knowledge eliminates the overhead of consensus-seeking on low-stakes decisions while preserving joint approval for big strategic calls.
bounded_by: Only applies to strategic decisions where expertise genuinely differs
Does not work if domain boundaries are unclear or contested

claims.text: Rory Sutherland unilaterally decided to build a software company despite his wife Layla's strong objection that it was the wrong time; this turned out to be a strategic error because the company consumed attention from gym launch and prestige labs (both performing well), created opportunity costs, lacked necessary infrastructure and team, and Layla was ultimately proven right—though she never 'rubbed it in'.
claims.speaker: Rory Sutherland
conditions: founder has multiple successful revenue streams already operating
spouse/co-founder explicitly objects to new venture on timing grounds
claims.mechanism: Founder conviction, even when wrong, can steamroll partner objections; the cost is opportunity loss on existing businesses and damaged team morale from diffuse attention.
bounded_by: Does not address cases where unilateral founder decision proved correct despite objection
Does not establish whether Layla's objection was about the business itself or the timing

claims.text: Rory and Layla have had only one major business-related argument in their entire marriage, suggesting that proactive communication and domain-specific decision authority dramatically reduce conflict frequency in working couples.
claims.speaker: Rory Sutherland
conditions: married couple working together full-time for multiple years
claims.mechanism: Low conflict frequency likely results from: (1) domain-specific authority eliminating consensus-seeking overhead, (2) proactive communication catching imbalances before resentment hardens, (3) absence of judgment about work/life balance creates psychological safety to raise issues early.

anchors.region: Rory and Layla (working couples with domain authority + proactive communication)
anchors.value: 1 major argument across entire marriage duration

bounded_by: Sample size is 1 couple; no comparison group provided
Does not distinguish whether low frequency is cause or effect of a strong relationship
Does not quantify 'minor' arguments that might be frequent

examples.text: When Rory proposed joining his business on their first date, he propositioned Layla repeatedly over 21 consecutive days (every time he saw her). After three weeks of daily pitches, Layla agreed to quit her job and join him. This early intimacy—recruiting her into the business before establishing romantic partnership norms—established a working relationship foundation before the couple had to navigate the conflict between professional and personal intimacy.

Rory decided to build a software company despite Layla's objection that the timing was wrong and the company would stretch their team too thin. Rory pushed forward because he believed the vision was bigger, but deployed himself entirely to the new venture while Layla spread herself across three businesses (gym launch, prestige labs, and the software company). The software company 'did okay' but the opportunity costs were substantial: attention diverted from gym launch and prestige labs, both of which were performing well. Layla was proven right about the timing mistake—though she never emphasized that fact.

Layla maintains an 11-year unbroken fitness-tracking streak (logging food every day without missing), demonstrating extreme discipline. On day 11 years, she decided to break the streak, reasoning that she'd proven to herself she understood her nutrition and could stop logging. Rory noted that the app company (MyFitnessPal) did not recognize or celebrate this achievement—a missed opportunity to identify a high-commitment user and engage her as a VIP.

practices.text: If you notice your relationship quality declining while working together, explicitly ask for dedicated 'us time' rather than hoping your partner notices.
When your partner makes a request related to the relationship (more time together, less work focus), concede immediately rather than defending the current work distribution.

Assign decision authority by domain expertise: let your partner make the call on decisions where they have better information or relationships, rather than seeking consensus on every operational choice.
